ground_truth.unit: dollars per month (household earnings per capita)
ground_truth.location: Table 5, column 1 (Household Earnings per Capita, Levels, bandwidth 300)
ground_truth.context: Table 5 ("Impact of Ownership Type on Earnings and Earnings Distributions"), column 1.  Regression discontinuity at the 1980 land reform's 500 ha cumulative-landholding threshold: properties of former owners above 500 ha became worker cooperatives, those below stayed outside-owned haciendas.  Outcome: household earnings per capita in the previous month, in dollars per month, of agricultural workers in the El Salvador household surveys (Encuesta de Hogares de Propositos Multiples, 2002-2013), matched to cooperatives and haciendas through the survey's questions on working as a cooperative member or hacienda laborer (matching limited to cantons with only one cooperative/large hacienda).  Regressor: Above500, an indicator for the property's former owner having over 500 ha in cumulative landholdings in 1980.  Linear control in the former owner's total landholdings estimated separately on each side of the cutoff (equation 1), sample limited to properties within 300 ha of the threshold, survey-round fixed effects, standard errors clustered at the former-owner level.  Observations are workers; the table also reports the number of properties, the number of clusters and the mean of the dependent variable.

i4r.notes: DP20 Table 3 col 3 (corrected data, duplicates removed): 13.21 (SE 32.35), N = 1,146 workers, p = 0.684 — the point estimate drops by ~three-quarters and loses significance.  Meta-database row labels this "duplicates AND sample restriction", but DP20's table is the duplicates-only correction (the five-member rule does not apply to the worker-level regression).

Observations are workers.  Not statistically significant.

ground_truth.unit: dollars per month (interquartile range of household earnings per capita)
ground_truth.location: Table 5, column 3 (Household Earnings per Capita, Interquartile Range, bandwidth 300)
ground_truth.context: Table 5, column 3, the paper's inequality result (a lower within-property interquartile range of earnings for cooperatives). Outcome: the interquartile range (75th minus 25th percentile) of household earnings per capita in the previous month across the surveyed workers of each property, with the sample limited to cooperatives and haciendas for which there are at least five members represented in the household surveys.  Regressor Above500; linear control in the former owner's landholdings on each side of the 500 ha cutoff; properties within 300 ha of the threshold; survey-round fixed effects; standard errors clustered at the former-owner level.  One observation per property.

i4r.notes: DP20 Table 1 col 3 (corrected data, duplicates removed, no five-member restriction, as in the original code): -72.24 (SE 17.37), N = 324.  Imposing the paper's stated five-member restriction instead: on the original data -50.91 (43.09), N = 128 with 3 treated property-years, p = 0.243 (col 5); on the corrected data -65.81 (45.36), N = 70 with 1 treated property-year (col 7) — DP20 concludes the data cannot support the analysis.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=20.3213 vs claimed=-42.97 (relative error 147.29%, tolerance 41.47%, the ±1·SE band with SE=17.82).
